slides.say: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all four sides equal. Its opposite angles are equal too.

A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal. So, like every parallelogram, its opposite sides are equal and parallel, and on top of that, all four sides are equal. In the quadrilaterals lesson, we shortened a parallelogram until all its sides were equal, and that gave us a rhombus.
at: its opposite sides are equal and parallel

slides.say: For example, a rhombus with side seven has a perimeter of four times seven, twenty-eight. And if one angle is sixty degrees, the opposite angle is sixty too, and the other two are one hundred twenty each, because two angles next to each other add up to one hundred eighty, like in every parallelogram.
Now the diagonals. They're perpendicular to each other, so they meet at a right angle.
Are they equal? Not necessarily. Usually there's a long diagonal and a short one, like here. Only if the two diagonals are equal, the rhombus is a square, like this one.
Let's go back to our rhombus. Its diagonals cut each other in half, and they also cut the angles of the rhombus in half.
Instead of remembering all these rules, the sides, the angles and the diagonals, just remember the shape, and remember that it's symmetric.

The diagonal A C is a line of symmetry. Fold along it, and the triangle on the right lands exactly on the triangle on the left. So the sides up here are equal, the sides down here are equal, and the angle on the right equals the angle on the left.
at: The diagonal A C is a line of symmetry

slides.say: And the other diagonal, B D, is a line of symmetry too. Fold along it, and the top triangle lands exactly on the bottom one. So the top angle equals the bottom angle.
So all the sides are equal, opposite angles are equal, and the diagonals are perpendicular, cut each other in half, and cut the angles in half.
at: So all the sides are equal

slides.say: The area of a rhombus is the product of the diagonals, over two. Why? The diagonals meet at ninety degrees, and they cut each other in half. So they split the rhombus into four equal right triangles. Look at one of them. Its legs are half of one diagonal and half of the other.

Its area is leg times leg, over two. Half of one diagonal times half of the other is the product of the diagonals, over four. Then we divide by two, so one triangle is the product of the diagonals, over eight.
at: product of the diagonals, over eight

slides.say: The rhombus is four of these triangles, so we multiply by four. Four times that is the product of the diagonals, over two. That's diagonal times diagonal, over two.
Let's see it in numbers, with diagonals twelve and eight. The legs of one small triangle are six and four. Its area is four times six over two, which is twelve.
at: The legs of one small triangle
Its area is four times six

slides.say: Four triangles make four times twelve, forty-eight. And with the formula, eight times twelve is ninety-six, and ninety-six over two is forty-eight too.
Another one, diagonals ten and six. Ten times six is sixty, and sixty over two is thirty.
